Load it with ToolSearch (select:Artifact) before writing any document, plan, analysis or visual, and whenever other people come up as readers, even after the work is written. Its description says whether to publish, offer a page or do neither. What follows applies whether or not it is loaded yet. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it.

A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). <?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. - animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
- apple-design: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
- emil-design-eng: This skill encodes Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design, animation decisions, and the invisible details that make software feel great.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- self-code-review: Deep, evidence-based self review of the current branch against its base. Use when the user asks to "self review", "review my branch", "review my PR", "review my code", "review my changes", or wants a thorough pre-push critique.

  works. Never trade a working product for unfinished complexity.

  complexity or improve reliability. Do not reimplement common
  functionality without a clear reason.
- Lean on the dependencies already in the project before writing your own
  implementation or adding packages. Do not assume a library lacks a
  capability without checking its documentation and types.
- Make architectural decisions for the long term. Do not accept a stopgap
  that only works for now and is meant to be replaced later.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Terse by default: after an action, state what changed in three lines or
  fewer. Explain only when asked.
- Surface non-trivial design decisions before baking them into a plan or an
  implementation.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

- [Research scope: own commits only](research-scope-own-commits.md): consolidating "my research" means Steffen's commits and sessions, not teammates' branches
- [Shared working tree](shared-working-tree.md) — peer sessions commit in the same checkout; re-check git state, never leave temporary constant edits
- [Elicit worktree](elicit-worktree.md) — experiments live in ../ehlcodacabana-elicit on branch steffen/elicit (PR #14), not in the shared checkout

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

input.description: Audit buyer code for dead code
input.prompt:
Read-only audit of /Users/stef/Projects/ehlcodacabana-final (Python 3.12, uv). Do NOT edit anything. Goal: find cleanup candidates in the `buyer/` package and `tests/`.

Context: `buyer/` is a negotiation agent wrapping the library `arena_kit` (installed in `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/arena_kit/`). Repo rules: no backward-compat layers, no speculative abstractions, wrap arena_kit rather than reimplement it.

Check and report, each with file:line evidence:
1. Unused functions, classes, constants, parameters, imports in buyer/*.py (grep every top-level def/const name across buyer/, tests/, analysis/ to confirm it is unused). Also try `uv run ruff check . --select F401,F841,ARG` and `uv run vulture buyer tests --min-confidence 60` if vulture is available via `uv run --with vulture vulture ...`.
2. Tiny modules that could be merged (buyer/agent.py 20 lines, buyer/reader.py 25 lines): what do they do, who imports them?
3. Code in buyer/ that reimplements something arena_kit already provides (look at arena_kit's public functions: total_cost, must_haves_ok, quote parsing, docs.standard_terms, runners, data lookup). Name the arena_kit function that would replace it.
4. Obsolete paths: fallbacks, compat shims, flags or CLI options in buyer/cli.py that look unused, commented-out code, TODOs.
5. Duplicated logic across modules (policy.py is 644 lines, claims.py 331).
6. Tests: run `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run ruff check .` and report results; note any test that tests removed behaviour or duplicates another.

Output: a concise list of findings grouped by the 6 headings, each with file:line, what, and suggested action (delete / merge / replace with arena_kit.X). Mark confidence high/medium/low. No preamble.

content.content:
1	"""The negotiation policy, per supplier thread: plan the non-price terms by C at the supplier's
2	own valuation, open below its quote, then move toward its counter round by round so it keeps
3	conceding, with verified claims spread over the rounds. Close on its final offer, its agreement or
4	the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.
5	
6	What the suppliers showed (sandbox and practice, `docs/learnings.md`):
7	- they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they
8	  would make, so our sheet stays below their counter until the end;
9	- every verified claim they take into account lowers where they stop, most of it in round 1;
10	- patience runs out at a cumulative gap of about 40 % between our sheets and their counters
11	  (summed per round, relative to their price), much earlier for a supplier selling near its cost
12	  or one that is fully booked: a final offer, or a walk-away;
13	- a large first concession means a deep floor: then we hold low instead of meeting it."""
14	
15	import base64
16	import functools
17	import logging
18	import time
19	
20	from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
21	from arena_kit.play import latest, moves_left, standing
22	
23	from . import economics as eco
24	from . import llm, reader, writer
25	from .claims import ClaimBank, rival_offer
26	from .personas import profile, signals_in
27	
28	log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
29	
30	FRACTION = 0.3  # share of the gap to the supplier's counter we move per round
31	# Opening price as a share of its quote at our terms, by category goal. Practice C_best sat 12 to
32	# 22 % below the quote in leverage, routine and secure-supply cases, 1.5 to 3 % in stabilise ones.
33	ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.78, "routine": 0.82, "secure_supply": 0.88, "quality_first": 0.88, "stabilise": 0.92}
34	ANCHOR_MIN = 0.75  # never open lower than this share (an insult costs patience)
35	BUDGET = 1.0  # patience: the cumulative relative gap we show (no cap for a typical supplier)
36	DEEP = 0.06  # a first concession this large (share of its quote) means a deep floor
37	MIN_MOVE = 0.002  # every sheet moves at least this share of the price
38	FIRST_CLAIMS, LATER_CLAIMS = 3, 1
39	DONE = {"agreed", "final_offer"}
40	ENDED = {"walked_away", "no_bid"}
41	
42	
43	class Side:
44	    """One supplier thread: what we know and what we did."""
45	
46	    def __init__(self, sid):
47	        self.sid = sid
48	        self.std = {}
49	        self.prof = {}
50	        self.est = {}
51	        self.terms = {}  # our planned non-price terms (with a price placeholder)
52	        self.quote = None  # its opening price at our terms
53	        self.last_sheet = {}  # its previous standing terms
54	        self.late = 0  # our messages the arena counted as rounds although they came too late
55	        self.anchor = None
56	        self.target = None  # relationship goals: the price with the lowest C
57	        self.budget = BUDGET
58	        self.claims = []
59	        self.ours = []  # our prices at s.terms, one per message with a sheet
60	        self.theirs = []  # its price at our terms, one per reply
61	        self.gaps = []  # relative gap of each of our sheets to its counter
62	        self.state = "open"  # open | mirror | closing | done | ended
63	        self.prev_state = "open"  # the state before the message in flight
64	        self.pending = None  # the message in flight: what to undo if it times out
65	        self.tried = set()  # (field, value) we switched away from
66	        self.term_change = False  # its last counter changed our non-price terms
67	        self.last_reply = None
68	        self.asks = []  # what its last e-mail asked of us (reader.asks)
69	        self.attached = set()  # files we already sent it
70	
71	
72	class Negotiator:
73	    def __init__(self, case, pkg=None, complete=None):
74	        self.case, self.pkg, self.complete = case, pkg, complete
75	        self.bank = ClaimBank(pkg, case)
76	        self.sides = {}
77	        self.used = set()  # claim IDs cited in this case (a rival quote: per supplier)
78	        self.notes = []  # what we decided, for the log
79	        self.writer_s = llm.TIMEOUT_S  # wall clock the model may take on the move being built
80	
81	    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
82	    def setup(self, sid, events):
83	        case, s = self.case, Side(sid)
84	        s.std = safe(lambda: standard_terms(events), {}) or {}
85	        sheet_id, quote = standing(events)
86	        s.prof = safe(lambda: profile(self.pkg, sid), profile(None, sid))
87	        self.read_signals(s, latest(events).get("body"))
88	        self.sides[sid] = s
89	        if not sheet_id or quote.get("unit_price") is None:
90	            s.state = "ended"
91	            return s
92	        s.last_sheet = quote
93	        # a bundle's should-cost is unknown: one component's cost is not the price unit of the kit
94	        parts = case.get("parts") or []
95	        full_cost, own_plant = (
96	            safe(lambda: self.full_cost(parts[0], sid), (None, False)) if len(parts) == 1 else (None, False)
97	        )
98	        lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
99	        overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
100	        s.est = eco.estimate(
101	            case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, safe(lambda: self.real_ppm(sid)), lead, overtime
102	        )
103	        q_price = quote["unit_price"]
104	        goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
105	        sustainable = case["buyer"].get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
106	        if full_cost and goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
107	            # it quoted with its margin: a should-cost above that is our estimate's error (P02: 374.95
108	            # against a quote of 370.96; the relationship charge of the deals says about 368)
109	            full_cost = min(full_cost, eco.value(case, quote, s.est) * (1 - sustainable / 100))
110	            s.est["full_cost"] = full_cost
111	        ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
112	        near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
113	        if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
114	            s.budget = 0.3
115	        if "price_frozen" in signals:
116	            ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
117	        if "capacity_full" in signals:
118	            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
119	        if near_cost:
120	            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
121	        current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
122	        if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
123	            ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
124	        ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
125	        # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
126	        planned = safe(lambda: eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio))
127	        s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.complete_offer(case, eco.at_price(case, quote, q_price * ratio))
128	        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
129	        s.quote = safe(
130	            lambda: round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2), q_price
131	        )
132	        if full_cost and not near_cost:
133	            s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
134	        safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
135	        s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
136	        self.note(
137	            sid,
138	            "setup",
139	            quote=quote,
140	            std=s.std,
141	            profile=s.prof,
142	            full_cost=full_cost,
143	            near_cost=near_cost,
144	            terms=s.terms,
145	            quote_at_terms=s.quote,
146	            anchor=s.anchor,
147	            target=s.target,
148	            budget=s.budget,
149	            claims=[c["text"] for c in s.claims],
150	        )
151	        return s

153	    def trade_clause(self, s, quote, full_cost):
154	        """An index clause the supplier values more than it costs us (its driver rose over the
155	        year, the case's path is small): offer it from the start at the price worth the same to it
156	        as our anchor without it, and in a relationship goal no lower than the relationship
157	        optimum, where it is agreed at once (P02: Nordmark agreed to a 5 % copper deadband 4 %
158	        below its fixed price). No trade where its value equals our cost (P08, P18)."""
159	        case = self.case
160	        if "index_clause" not in case["negotiable"] or quote.get("index_clause"):
161	            return
162	        for clause in case.get("term_options", {}).get("index_clause") or []:
163	            if clause and clause.get("series") not in s.est["index_moves"]:
164	                move = self.bank.move12(clause["series"])
165	                if move is not None:
166	                    s.est["index_moves"][clause["series"]] = move
167	        clause = eco.clause_trade(case, s.est)
168	        if not clause or s.terms.get("index_clause") == clause:
169	            return
170	        target_value = eco.value(case, s.terms, s.est)  # our anchor as it is worth to the supplier
171	        terms = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
172	        price = eco.price_for_value(case, terms, s.est, target_value)
173	        floor = None
174	        if full_cost and case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
175	            floor = eco.relationship_optimum(case, terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote)
176	            price = max(price, floor or 0.0)
177	        if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, eco.at_price(case, terms, price), s.std):
178	            return
179	        s.terms = eco.at_price(case, terms, price)
180	        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
181	        s.target = floor or s.target
182	        self.note(s.sid, "clause_trade", clause=clause, anchor=s.anchor, target=s.target)
183	
184	    def full_cost(self, part, sid):
185	        """(should-cost of the part, whether it models this supplier's own plant): full cost
186	        without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""
187	        rows = self.bank.query("SELECT id, supplier_id, unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
188	        own = [r for r in rows if r.get("supplier_id") == sid]
189	        if own:
190	            return own[0]["unit_cost"], True
191	        generic = [r for r in rows if not r.get("supplier_id")]
192	        if generic:
193	            return generic[0]["unit_cost"], False
194	        for ref in self.bank.ids("cost:"):  # the case's own facts (no table rows)
195	            f = self.bank.fact(ref)
196	            if f and f.get("part") == part and f.get("unit_cost"):
197	                return f["unit_cost"], f.get("supplier") == sid
198	        return None, False

202	        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
203	        f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
204	        return f.get("ppm") if f else None

206	    def restore(self, sid, events):
207	        """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
208	        the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
209	        s = self.sides[sid]
210	        ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
211	        if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
212	            return
213	        s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
214	        theirs = None
215	        for m in events:
216	            if m.get("from") == "buyer":
217	                self.used.update(m.get("refs") or [])
218	                if m.get("term_sheets"):
219	                    price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
220	                    s.ours.append(price)
221	                    s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
222	            else:
223	                sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
224	                if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
225	                    theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
226	                    if s.ours:
227	                        s.theirs.append(theirs)
228	        if events and events[-1].get("from") != "buyer" and s.theirs:
229	            s.theirs.pop()  # the latest reply is read by move() like any fresh reply
230	        self.note(sid, "restore", ours=s.ours, theirs=s.theirs, terms=s.terms)

233	    def read_signals(self, s, body):
234	        """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
235	        merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""
236	        new = [k for k in signals_in(body) if k not in s.prof["signals"]]
237	        if not new:
238	            return
239	        s.prof["signals"] = sorted(s.prof["signals"] + new)
240	        if "cash_need" in new:
241	            s.prof["rate"] = round(s.prof["rate"] + 0.05, 3)
242	            if s.est:
243	                s.est["interest_rate"] = s.prof["rate"]
244	        self.note(s.sid, "signals", new=new)

246	    def their_price(self, s, terms):
247	        """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
248	        same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
249	        if same:
250	            return terms["unit_price"]
251	        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
252	        return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)
253	
254	    def switch(self, s, new, why):
255	        """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
256	        if s.ours:
257	            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
258	            s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
259	        if s.theirs:
260	            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
261	            s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
262	        s.terms = {**new}
263	        self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})
264	
265	    def adopt(self, s, sheets):
266	        """Its reply changed some of our non-price terms (in its counter or an alternative): it told
267	        us what it values. Take a sheet's terms over when C at its price beats C of our plan at
268	        our counterpart of that price; when it insists on an index clause, take the clause that
269	        costs us least."""
270	        if not s.ours:
271	            return
272	        case = self.case
273	        standing_terms = sheets[0]["terms"]
274	        clause = standing_terms.get("index_clause")
275	        if "index_clause" in s.terms and s.terms["index_clause"] != clause and clause:
276	            # it will not sell this term at a fixed price (raw-material distributors) and refuses a
277	            # deadband: take its clause when its sheet, clause included, costs us less than its
278	            # last one (P08, P18: a longer contract came with it) and keeps every must-have; else
279	            # keep asking for a fixed price (P02: the copper clause alone cost 1.8 % of spend)
280	            new = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
281	            c_now = eco.cost(case, standing_terms, s.std, s.est)
282	            c_before = eco.cost(case, s.last_sheet, s.std, s.est)
283	            if eco.must_haves_ok(case, new, s.std) and c_now < c_before - 1.0:
284	                self.switch(s, new, "its index clause")
285	            else:
286	                self.note(s.sid, "keep_terms", why="its index clause costs us more", c_now=c_now, c_before=c_before)
287	        best_c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing_terms)), s.std, s.est)
288	        for sheet in sheets:
289	            terms = sheet["terms"]
290	            changed = {k: v for k, v in terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in s.terms and s.terms[k] != v}
291	            changed.pop("index_clause", None)
292	            if not changed:
293	                continue
294	            new = {**s.terms, **changed}
295	            if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, new, s.std):
296	                continue
297	            if any((k, repr(v)) in s.tried for k, v in changed.items()):
298	                continue  # we were there before: no flip-flop
299	            c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, new, terms["unit_price"]), s.std, s.est)
300	            if c < best_c - max(1.0, 0.001 * best_c):
301	                best_c = c
302	                s.tried |= {(k, repr(s.terms.get(k))) for k in changed}
303	                self.switch(s, new, f"its sheet {changed} costs us less")
304	
305	    # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
306	    def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
307	        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
308	        `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
309	        case, s, events = self.case, self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
310	        self.writer_s = writer_s
311	        s.prev_state = s.state
312	        last = latest(events)
313	        status = last.get("status")
314	        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
315	            s.state = "ended"
316	            return None
317	        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
318	        if not sheets:
319	            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
320	            return None
321	        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
322	        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
323	        if fresh:
324	            terms_before = dict(s.terms)
325	            self.adopt(s, sheets)
326	            s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
327	            s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
328	            s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
329	            s.last_reply = last
330	            s.asks = reader.asks(last.get("body"))
331	            self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
332	        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
333	        if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
334	            s.state = "done"
335	            return None
336	        left = self.moves_left(s, events)
337	        if status in DONE or left <= 0:
338	            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
339	        if s.target and theirs <= s.target * 1.002:
340	            # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
341	            s.state = "closing"
342	            return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))], [], events, theirs)
343	        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
344	            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
345	        price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
346	        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
347	        return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, price)], claims, events, theirs)
348	
349	    def moves_left(self, s, events):
350	        """Messages we may still send: the arena counts a late message as a round too."""
351	        return moves_left(self.case, events) - s.late
352	
353	    def next_price(self, s, theirs):
354	        """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
355	        large concession, and within the patience budget."""
356	        if not s.ours:
357	            return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS
358	        last = s.ours[-1]
359	        gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
360	        conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
361	        share = FRACTION
362	        if len(s.ours) == 1 and conceded >= DEEP and not s.term_change:
363	            # a deep floor: a pure price drop this large means it moves fast on its own (job shops,
364	            # P05, D02) and agrees at our sheet next: hold the anchor (Dralveck agreed at a held
365	            # 27.86, at 28.07 after an 8 % step); a drop that came with terms it added (an index
366	            # clause, P08, P18) is not one
367	            share = 0.0
368	        left = max(0.0, s.budget - sum(s.gaps))
369	        new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
370	        if s.budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
371	            new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
372	        price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
373	        price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
374	        price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
375	        return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS
376	
377	    def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):
378	        """Its final word, its agreement or our last message: if one of its alternatives costs us
379	        less than its standing sheet, send that sheet back so it agrees to it; else done."""
380	        case = self.case
381	        std = s.std
382	        c_stand = eco.cost(case, sheets[0]["terms"], std, s.est)
383	        alts = [(eco.cost(case, sh["terms"], std, s.est), sh) for sh in sheets[1:]]
384	        alts = [(c, sh) for c, sh in alts if eco.must_haves_ok(case, sh["terms"], std)]
385	        if alts and left > 0:
386	            c, sh = min(alts, key=lambda r: r[0])
387	            if c < c_stand - 1.0:
388	                s.state = "mirror"
389	                terms = {k: v for k, v in sh["terms"].items() if k in case["negotiable"]}
390	                return self.send(s, [eco.complete_offer(case, terms)], [], events, theirs)
391	        s.state = "done"
392	        return None

394	    def pick(self, s, n, threads):
395	        """The next unused claims for this supplier: in an RFQ the cheapest rival offer first (a new
396	        offer is a new argument every round), then its own claims, strongest first."""
397	        out = []
398	        rivals = []
399	        for other, events in threads.items():
400	            if other == s.sid or latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
401	                continue
402	            oid, t = standing(events)
403	            if oid and t.get("unit_price") and s.theirs:
404	                price = self.their_price(s, t)
405	                if price < s.theirs[-1]:
406	                    rivals.append((price, rival_offer(other, oid, t["unit_price"])))
407	        pool = [c for _, c in sorted(rivals, key=lambda r: r[0])[:1]] + s.claims
408	        for c in pool:
409	            key = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for i in c["ids"]]
410	            if any(k in self.used for k in key):
411	                continue
412	            out.append(c)
413	            if len(out) >= n:
414	                break
415	        return out

495	    def send(self, s, sheets, claims, events, theirs):
496	        first = not s.ours
497	        moved = len(s.theirs) > 1 and s.theirs[-1] < s.theirs[-2] - 0.005
498	        price = sheets[0]["unit_price"]
499	        keys = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for c in claims for i in c["ids"]]
500	        s.pending = {"state": s.prev_state, "keys": keys}
501	        statements = self.statements(s, sheets)
502	        attachments = self.attachments(s)
503	        if s.state not in ("mirror",):
504	            s.ours.append(price)
505	            s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
506	            s.pending["appended"] = True
507	        tone = "warm" if s.prof.get("warm", True) else "friendly and businesslike"
508	        facts = self.facts(s, sheets, claims, moved, statements, attachments)
509	        para = llm.paragraph(
510	            self.complete,
511	            writer.brief(self.case, s.prof, latest(events).get("body"), facts, tone, first),
512	            self.writer_s,
513	        )
514	        body = writer.email(
515	            self.case,
516	            sheets,
517	            claims,
518	            statements,
519	            first=first,
520	            moved=moved,
521	            warm=s.prof.get("warm", True),
522	            paragraph=para,
523	        )
524	        refs = sorted({i for c in claims for i in c["ids"]})
525	        self.note(
526	            s.sid,
527	            "send",
528	            state=s.state,
529	            theirs=theirs,
530	            ours=price,
531	            claims=[c["kind"] for c in claims],
532	            asks=s.asks,
533	            attached=[a["name"] for a in attachments],
534	        )
535	        message = {
536	            "subject": reply_subject(events, self.case),
537	            "body": body,
538	            "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
539	            "refs": refs,
540	        }
541	        if attachments:
542	            message["attachments"] = attachments
543	        return {"message": message}
544	
545	    def fallback_move(self, sid, threads):
546	        """After an error in move(): our last sheet again with the template e-mail, so the thread
547	        never falls silent; without a sheet of ours yet, a short question."""
548	        s = self.sides.get(sid)
549	        events = threads[sid]
550	        if not s or not s.ours or not s.terms:
551	            return {"message": keepalive_message(events)}
552	        sheets = [eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.ours[-1])]
553	        body = writer.email(self.case, sheets, [], [], warm=s.prof.get("warm", True))
554	        self.note(sid, "fallback", ours=s.ours[-1])
555	        return {
556	            "message": {
557	                "subject": reply_subject(events, self.case),
558	                "body": body,
559	                "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
560	                "refs": [],
561	            }
562	        }
563	
564	    def commit(self, sid):
565	        """The message reached the supplier: its claims are spent."""
566	        s = self.sides[sid]
567	        if s.pending:
568	            self.used.update(s.pending["keys"])
569	            s.pending = None
570	
571	    def rollback(self, sid):
572	        """The message came too late (a timeout): the supplier never read it."""
573	        s = self.sides[sid]
574	        if s.pending:
575	            if s.pending.get("appended"):
576	                s.ours.pop()
577	                s.gaps.pop()
578	            s.state = s.pending["state"]
579	            s.pending = None
580	            s.late += 1
581	            self.note(sid, "rollback", late=s.late)
582	
583	    # -- close -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
584	    def best_offer(self, threads):
585	        """(C, supplier, term_sheet_id) of the cheapest acceptable standing sheet (only a standing
586	        sheet can be accepted; alternatives were sent back to become standing). One supplier's
587	        broken data skips that supplier, never the close."""
588	        best = None
589	        for sid, events in threads.items():
590	            if latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
591	                continue
592	            oid, terms = standing(events)
593	            c = safe(functools.partial(self.deal_cost, sid, events, terms)) if oid else None
594	            if c is not None and (best is None or c < best[0]):
595	                best = (c, sid, oid)
596	        return best
597	
598	    def deal_cost(self, sid, events, terms):
599	        side = self.sides.get(sid) or Side(sid)
600	        return eco.deal_cost(self.case, terms, standard_terms(events) or side.std, side.est)
601	
602	    def close(self, threads):
603	        best = self.best_offer(threads)
604	        if best is None:
605	            live = [sid for sid, ev in threads.items() if latest(ev).get("status") not in ENDED] or list(threads)
606	            self.note(None, "walk_away")
607	            return {"supplier_id": live[0], "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
608	        self.note(best[1], "accept", c=best[0], offer=best[2])
609	        return {"supplier_id": best[1], "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": best[2]}}}

613	        self.notes.append(entry)
614	        log.info(

616	            self.case["case_id"],
617	            sid,
618	            {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k not in ("claims", "std", "profile")},
619	        )

623	    """`fn()`, or `default` when it raises: a hidden case may lack a field the data code expects,
624	    and a missing claim or profile must never cost the move."""
